relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: all antisense treatments resulted in significantly higher nociceptive thresholds when compared to the corresponding mismatch groups (p < 0.05)

relationships.subject: TNF-α
relationships.evidence_quote: It also significantly reduced the upregulation of Nav1.8 mRNA (Figure 4B; p < 0.05) in the first and second days after surgery

relationships.subject: p38 MAPK
relationships.evidence_quote: Both the NF-kB antagonist PDTC at 100 mg/kg and the p38 antagonist SB203580 at 20 mg/kg reduced the hyperexpression of Nav1.8 (Figure 5E; p < 0.05) and Nav1.9 (Figure 5F; p < 0.05) in the DRG.

relationships.subject: NF-κB
relationships.evidence_quote: The treatment with the NF-kB antagonist PDTC (100 mg/kg, intraperitoneally) significantly reduced the expression of TNF-α mRNA (Figure 6A) and COX-2 mRNA (Figure 6B) in the DRG

relationships.subject: COX-2
relationships.evidence_quote: Since COX-2 mRNA was upregulated in the DRG, it is likely that this cyclooxygenase isoform contributed to plantar PGE2 synthesis.

key_findings: Plantar incision upregulated Nav1.8 and Nav1.9 in DRG; antisense knockdown reduced hypernociception.
TNF-α, p38 and NF-κB (but not COX inhibition, ERK or JNK) drive Nav1.8/Nav1.9 upregulation and hypernociception.
